extracted.intended_audience: Users of GAP (mathematicians, computational group theorists, and programmers using GAP for permutation and permutation-group computations)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for GAP functions, attributes, and algorithms relating to permutations, external sets, actions, permutation groups, and stabilizer-chain construction; includes definitions, input requirements, options, and performance guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: CanonicalRepresentativeDeterminatorOfExternalSet
rubrics_metrics.description: An external set has an attribute CanonicalRepresentativeDeterminatorOfExternalSet(xset) which returns a function taking an acting group and a point and returning a list (length 1 or 3) whose first entry is the canonical representative; other entries (if present) are the stabilizer and a conjugating element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An external set is only guaranteed to be able to compute a canonical representative if it has this attribute (i.e., the presence of this attribute is required to compute canonical representatives).

rubrics_metrics.name: ActorOfExternalSet
rubrics_metrics.description: ActorOfExternalSet(xset) returns an element mapping Representative(xset) to CanonicalRepresentativeOfExternalSet(xset) under the given action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to obtain the element of the acting group which realizes the canonical representative mapping; examples show usage with cosets and FunctionAction to apply the actor.

rubrics_metrics.name: UnderlyingExternalSet
rubrics_metrics.description: UnderlyingExternalSet(acthom) returns the external set on which the action homomorphism acthom was defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to access and print the underlying list or collection of points for an action homomorphism (examples show printing arrangement tuples).

rubrics_metrics.name: SurjectiveActionHomomorphismAttr
rubrics_metrics.description: SurjectiveActionHomomorphismAttr(xset) returns an action homomorphism for xset which is surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computing the Image (32.4.6) of this homomorphism to obtain the range may take substantially longer than ActionHomomorphism (41.7.1) because the image has to be computed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permutation internal degree and storage
rubrics_metrics.description: A permutation is stored internally as a list of the d images of 1..d where d (internal degree) is the largest integer moved by the permutation or larger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reading cycle notation d is set to largest moved integer, but multiplication may produce a larger d because the product is not shortened if it fixes d. Storage uses 16-bit or 32-bit integers depending on d (d ≤ 65536 uses 16-bit). Large d implies large memory (e.g., m-cycle uses ~4m bytes if 32-bit). Identity computed from a large-cycle representation can still occupy large storage. Use RestrictedPerm to reduce storage degree of results and save memory if intermediate calculations have large degree but final result has small degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: System degree limits and error handling
rubrics_metrics.description: On 32-bit systems the limit on permutation degree is 2^28 - 1; on 64-bit systems it is 2^32 - 1 (because a 32-bit integer is used internally for each image).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands that would require creating a permutation exceeding this limit should produce error messages; be aware of these architecture-dependent limits when constructing large permutations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permutations do not need a parent group
rubrics_metrics.description: Permutations do not belong to a specific group; one can work with permutations without defining a containing permutation group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many permutation operations are available directly; group-level optimizations apply only when groups are constructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of permutations (\=)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two permutations are equal if they move the same points and those points have the same images under both permutations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equality compares images of moved points; examples demonstrate equality of cycle notations that represent same mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order relation for permutations (<)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permutation p1 is smaller than p2 if p1 ≠ p2 and i^p1 < i^p2 where i is the smallest point with differing images; hence the identity permutation is the smallest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ordering is lexicographic on images of smallest differing point; examples illustrate comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: DistancePerms
rubrics_metrics.description: DistancePerms(perm1, perm2) returns the number of points for which perm1 and perm2 have different images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should always equal NrMovedPoints(perm1 /perm2) though some methods may compute it more efficiently since creating a new permutation can be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: SmallestGeneratorPerm
rubrics_metrics.description: SmallestGeneratorPerm(perm) returns the smallest permutation that generates the same cyclic group as perm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to be very efficient even when perm has large order; example: SmallestGeneratorPerm((1,4,3,2)) returns (1,2,3,4).

rubrics_metrics.name: SmallestMovedPoint / LargestMovedPoint
rubrics_metrics.description: SmallestMovedPoint(perm) is the smallest positive integer moved by perm (or infinity for identity). LargestMovedPoint(perm) is the largest positive integer moved by perm (or 0 for identity). For collections, returns min/max across elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these attributes to determine internal degree or ranges to pass to ListPerm etc.; examples show behavior on lists and empty collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: MovedPoints and NrMovedPoints
rubrics_metrics.description: MovedPoints(perm or C) returns the set of positive integers moved by at least one permutation in the input; NrMovedPoints returns the count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for orbit and degree computations; examples show lists of moved points and counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: PERM_INVERSE_THRESHOLD
rubrics_metrics.description: Global variable PERM_INVERSE_THRESHOLD: for permutations of degree up to this threshold the entire inverse is computed and stored; otherwise inverse is found by tracing the cycle of the point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threshold default is 10000; can be adjusted by assignment. Storing inverses saves time on subsequent computations at expense of memory; tracing cycles uses time when needed but saves memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: SignPerm
rubrics_metrics.description: SignPerm(perm) is defined as (-1)^k where k is the number of cycles of perm of even length; it is a homomorphism onto {+1,-1} whose kernel is the alternating group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to detect parity of permutations and alternate group membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: CycleStructurePerm
rubrics_metrics.description: CycleStructurePerm(perm) returns the cycle structure as a list l where l[i] contains the number of cycles of length i+1; cycles of length 1 are ignored and entries for absent cycle lengths are unbound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpreting returned list requires remembering index ⇄ cycle-length shift; examples given.

rubrics_metrics.name: ListPerm
rubrics_metrics.description: ListPerm(perm[, n]) returns list l with images of positive integers 1..n under perm (l[i] = i^perm). If n omitted, largest point moved by perm is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to view permutation as image list; specifying n can force output length or include fixed points up to n.

rubrics_metrics.name: PermList input validity
rubrics_metrics.description: PermList(list) returns the permutation π described by list where i^π = list[i] for i in 1..length(list), and fixes points beyond. PermList returns fail if 'list' does not define a permutation (i.e., list is not dense, contains duplicate integers, values outside 1..length(list), non-integers, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure list is a dense permutation image list before calling PermList to avoid fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: MappingPermListList compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: MappingPermListList(src, dst) returns a permutation π such that src[i]^π = dst[i] for all i, fixing points not in src or dst. Returns fail if no such permutation exists. If several permutations satisfy condition, which one is returned is unspecified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: src and dst must be lists of positive integers of same length and compatible with some permutation; do not rely on choice if non-unique.

rubrics_metrics.name: RestrictedPerm requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: RestrictedPerm(perm, list) returns the permutation acting on points in 'list' same as perm and fixing other points; 'list' must be the union of cycles of perm (i.e., for each i in list, i^perm must also be in list). The result is stored with internal degree = max(list).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RestrictedPerm to reduce storage degree. If you cannot guarantee 'list' is union of cycles, use RestrictedPermNC which does not check (but can produce incorrect result if precondition fails).

rubrics_metrics.name: RestrictedPermNC behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: RestrictedPermNC(perm, list) behaves like RestrictedPerm but does not check whether 'list' is a union of cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faster but unsafe if 'list' is not union of cycles; use only when caller guarantees precondition.

rubrics_metrics.name: CycleFromList preconditions
rubrics_metrics.description: CycleFromList(list) returns the n-cycle (a1,a2,...,an) for a given dense, duplicate-free list of positive integers. For empty list returns identity (). If list contains duplicates or holes, returns fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input must be dense and duplicate-free; examples show failing cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: AsPermutation conversion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: AsPermutation(f) converts partial permutations and transformations that mathematically define permutations into GAP permutations; returns a permutation or fail. For partial permutations, it returns the permutation of its image if f permutes its image; else fail. For transformations, returns permutation iff rank equals degree; else fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Permutation (41.9.1) as alternative converter when appropriate. Examples show PartialPerm and Transformation inputs and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPermGroup definition
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPermGroup(obj) marks permutation groups: groups of permutations on a finite set Ω of positive integers. GAP does not require specifying Ω when defining a permutation group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permutation groups inherit group operations and benefit from special methods for permutation groups in GAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural action applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions MovedPoints, NrMovedPoints, LargestMovedPoint, SmallestMovedPoint apply to arbitrary collections of permutations and thus to permutation groups; action functions like Orbit, Stabilizer, Blocks, IsTransitive, IsPrimitive apply to the natural action on positive integers via OnPoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For efficiency, special functions OrbitPerms and OrbitsPerms exist to compute orbits of generated groups from lists of generators without constructing the group explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsomorphismPermGroup behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: IsomorphismPermGroup(G) returns an isomorphism from group G onto a permutation group isomorphic to G; method selects a suitable permutation representation, often regular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to obtain a permutation representation for abstract groups; examples show mapping of pc-groups to permutations.

rubrics_metrics.name: SmallerDegreePermutationRepresentation purpose and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: SmallerDegreePermutationRepresentation(G) tries to find a faithful permutation representation of smaller degree for permutation group G; result is a group homomorphism onto a permutation group, worst case identity on G. If option 'cheap' is given it only tries reduce to orbits/blocks; otherwise also coset actions of random subgroups are tried.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result not guaranteed minimal or smallest among transitive reps; randomized methods may be used, so outputs/degree may vary between calls. Use interactive selection of small-index subgroups when possible. Option 'cheap' speeds up but may miss reductions; 'skip' returns identity mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetric/Alternating group detection
rubrics_metrics.description: IsNaturalSymmetricGroup(group) and IsNaturalAlternatingGroup(group) indicate whether group acts as symmetric/alternating group on its moved points. IsSymmetricGroup and IsAlternatingGroup return true if group is isomorphic to symmetric/alternating group (not necessarily natural).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If known natural symmetric/alternating groups are detected, very efficient methods for membership, conjugacy classes, Sylow subgroups, etc., are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: SymmetricParentGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: SymmetricParentGroup(grp) returns the symmetric group that moves the same points as permutation group grp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to obtain ambient symmetric group for computations and representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ONanScottType for primitive groups
rubrics_metrics.description: ONanScottType(G) returns the O'Nan-Scott classification type (string code) of a primitive permutation group G (labels follow Praeger conventions). If G is not a permutation group or not primitive, result is undefined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returned type is a string and may contain letters; documentation maps codes to names (Affine, AS, HS, SD, HC, CD, PA, TW).

rubrics_metrics.name: SocleTypePrimitiveGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: SocleTypePrimitiveGroup(G) returns the socle type of a primitive permutation group G as a record with series, parameter and width describing the direct product of isomorphic simple groups (socle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If G does not act primitively on its moved points, an error is returned; example shows record fields and usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stabilizer chain concepts (base, SGS, reduced)
rubrics_metrics.description: A stabilizer chain is defined by a base B = [b1,...,bn] with G(i+1)=Stab_{G(i)}(bi). A strong generating set (SGS) relative to B satisfies ⟨S ∩ G(i)⟩ = G(i). A base is reduced if no i has G(i)=G(i+1). Different reduced bases may have different lengths. The length of a base is number of points in it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every permutation group has a base (e.g., all moved points). Reduced bases are typical; base-change and storage choices impact algorithmic performance. Examples illustrate different reduced base lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factorized inverse transversals / Schreier trees storage goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Rather than storing full coset representatives (which can be many different permutations), GAP stores factorized inverse transversals (Schreier trees): T[p] is a generator such that pT[p] is earlier in O(i) than p, allowing construction of transversal elements by following tree edges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This minimizes the number of distinct stored permutations while allowing reconstruction of coset representatives; important for large degree groups to save memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomized methods for stabilizer chains
rubrics_metrics.description: For groups of degree > 100 GAP uses randomized heuristic algorithms (based on [BCFS91]) to construct stabilizer chains, complemented by a verification routine that either proves correctness or causes extension. The 'random' option (integer 1..1000) controls probabilistic guarantee: value x gives correctness probability at least x/1000; random=1000 uses a method guaranteeing correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default random=1000 is recommended. Using smaller random is useful to quickly find candidates across many subgroups or when tolerating probabilistic correctness. If group order is known and provided via 'size' or SetSize, construction can stop when product of orbit sizes equals order and be guaranteed correct—this is faster than full verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: StabChain function and options
rubrics_metrics.description: StabChain(G[, options]) computes a stabilizer chain for permutation group G. Options is a record controlling computation; if a base list is provided as second argument, it is interpreted as rec(base:=base).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If StabChainImmutable already stored and matches options, it may be returned. Default options come from DefaultStabChainOptions. Several supported options are documented below (base, knownBase, reduced, tryPcgs, random, size, limit).

rubrics_metrics.name: StabChain option: base
rubrics_metrics.description: options.base (default empty list) is a list of points through which resulting stabilizer chain should run. If reduced=true then only those points in base with nontrivial basic orbits form initial segment of resulting base; if reduced=false then base itself is the initial segment. Repeated occurrences ignored. If stabilizer chain already known, base change is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting base lets user control or force specific base points; use with reduced appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: StabChain option: knownBase
rubrics_metrics.description: options.knownBase (no default) is a list of points known to be a base for the group. This helps testing permutation words for identity more efficiently and speeds Schreier-Sims when constructing new stabilizer chains. It does not affect base changes and is independent of options.base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide knownBase when available to accelerate identity testing during construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: StabChain option: reduced
rubrics_metrics.description: options.reduced (default true) requests the resulting stabilizer chain to be reduced (no G(i)=G(i+1)). Setting reduced=false only makes sense when base is also set, in which case all points of base will occur in resulting base even if they have trivial basic orbits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default true usually desirable; use false only to force inclusion of specified base points.

rubrics_metrics.name: StabChain option: tryPcgs
rubrics_metrics.description: options.tryPcgs (default true) — if true and degree ≤100 or group known solvable, GAP first tries to construct a pcgs (polycyclic generating sequence) which implicitly constructs a stabilizer chain; if G turns out non-solvable another method is used. The solvability check is relatively cheap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaving true can save time for solvable groups; setting false skips this attempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: StabChain option: random
rubrics_metrics.description: options.random (default 1000) controls probabilistic verification: if value < 1000 the resulting chain is correct with probability at least random/1000; detailed behavior described in randomized methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default 1000 yields guaranteed correct verification (recommended); smaller values used for faster but probabilistic construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: StabChain option: size
rubrics_metrics.description: options.size (default Size(G) if known) if present is assumed to be order of G; this can be used to prove correctness of non-deterministically constructed stabilizer chain—GAP constructs until product of basic orbit lengths equals given size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing group order (via size or SetSize) speeds verification and gives guaranteed correct output.

rubrics_metrics.name: StabChain option: limit
rubrics_metrics.description: options.limit (default Size(Parent(G)) or StabChainOptions(Parent(G)).limit if present) must be >= |G| if given; stabilizer chain construction stops when size limit is reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to prevent uncontrolled computation; ensure limit large enough if expecting full chain.

rubrics_metrics.name: StabChainOptions attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: StabChainOptions(G) is an attribute storing the options record with which StabChainImmutable was computed for G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspecting this attribute reveals how the stored stabilizer chain was constructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: DefaultStabChainOptions global
rubrics_metrics.description: DefaultStabChainOptions is the global variable providing default options for StabChain when none are supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modify this global to change default behavior across sessions if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: StabChainBaseStrongGenerators
rubrics_metrics.description: StabChainBaseStrongGenerators(base, sgs[, one]) constructs a stabilizer chain for a given base and corresponding strong generating set without computing Schreier generators; one is the identity element (optional if sgs nonempty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is much faster than other algorithms when a base and SGS are already known.
